references.text: Before the years of famine came, Joseph's wife Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore him two sons. Joseph called the firstborn Manasseh, 'For,' he said, 'God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father's house.' The second he called Ephraim, 'For,' he said, 'God has made me fruitful in the land of my suffering.'
In Egypt, Joseph had sons Manasseh and Ephraim with Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.
Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the firstfruits of my youth – Jacob compares Ephraim and Manasseh to Reuben and Simeon, his two eldest sons.
Simeon and Levi are brothers – Simeon is explicitly mentioned in 48:5 as one of the sons with whom Ephraim and Manasseh are to be equated.
Joseph's sons formed two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim – fulfilling Jacob's adoption of them as his own sons.
The birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, son of Israel, and they were counted as tribes in Israel.
Genesis 48 establishes the tribal status of Ephraim and Manasseh as the basis for their inheritance in Joshua 16.
Genesis 46:8 identifies Reuben and Simeon as the eldest sons, giving meaning to the adoption comparison in 48:5.
Reuben is mentioned as the firstborn in 49:3, underscoring the significance of Ephraim and Manasseh being given equal status in 48:5.
Numbers 26:28 confirms the tribal status that Jacob established for Ephraim and Manasseh in Genesis 48:5.
